limitations: Three payments, one service, fixed per-request/daily limits and one forward day rollover.
The model follows X402Client reserved payments. Direct unreserved recordPayment calls, mutable service budget policies, on-chain limits and process restart are outside this model.
A transfer with unknown outcome retains its in-memory hold. Holds reset on process restart. Durable ledger behavior remains outside this model.
One pre-authorized signed transaction and abstract accepted/rejected/lost RPC responses.
Approval admission, signer isolation, actual chain execution and cross-process retry coordination need their own models and live tests.
Two known token addresses and two RPC endpoints; balances abstract to zero, nonzero or invalid, with valid or invalid uint8 decimals.
Provider promises and their continuations must eventually settle for progress. No wall-clock latency bound is proven.
Price enrichment, Alchemy/Ankr paths, external provider correctness and caller cancellation are outside this direct-RPC model.
The real loopback implementation tests cover the modeled observations; this finite model and those cases are not a full TypeScript refinement proof.
